sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-07 01:43 UTC. Scope: Daily. GitHub Trending date: 2026-11-07. Recent-created repository search window: 2026-11-05 through 2026-11-07 UTC. Ranking basis: daily Trending star gains, with one recent-created repository appended as a freshness signal.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-oriented skills and security workflows dominate the strongest daily spikes: Cloudflare's security-audit skill, Matt Pocock's engineering skills, and NVIDIA's Auto Ontology lead GitHub Trending. Alongside them, established editors, language tooling, frameworks, and infrastructure projects show broad developer-tool interest rather than a single-category surge.

sections.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
sections.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings.
sections.content: A coding-agent skill that coordinates multi-phase security audits and independently verified, structured findings.
sections.why_notable: It leads the daily list and exemplifies security review becoming a structured, auditable agent workflow.
sections.unique_caveat: The README calls for an OS-enforced sandbox with network restrictions and resource limits before executing target-controlled code.

enrichment.architecture_summary: An agent-orchestrated, six-phase audit pipeline builds a deterministic architecture and coverage ledger, dispatches isolated hunting agents, independently validates candidates and final source claims, and derives reports from structured findings.
enrichment.workflow: Reconnaissance -> coverage-led hunting -> candidate validation -> structured findings -> independent verification -> report generation.
enrichment.design_pattern: Adversarial verification with coverage tracking and machine-readable findings; confirmed, unresolved, and rejected candidates remain distinct.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
sections.content: A collection of small, composable agent skills for practical software engineering.
sections.why_notable: Its second-place daily gain signals strong demand for reusable, model-agnostic engineering workflows rather than one monolithic agent process.
sections.unique_caveat: The README notes installation/update behavior differs by agent; some integrations update automatically while others require manual refresh.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A repository of small, editable and composable engineering/productivity skills intended to be adapted and used across multiple coding agents.
core_components: manual install/update path for other agents
enrichment.workflow: Install the collection through an agent plugin or skills.sh, run setup in each repository, then invoke task-focused skills such as grilling or documentation workflows.
enrichment.design_pattern: Composable prompt/workflow modules instead of a single prescriptive end-to-end development process.

sections.title: NVIDIA/auto-ontology
sections.description: A Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data for LLM and agent workflows.
sections.content: A semantic context layer that grounds data and agent queries in enterprise metadata and certified definitions.
sections.why_notable: Its rapid rise points to a practical focus on trustworthy agentic analytics, provenance, and query validation.
sections.unique_caveat: The README states that external contributions are not currently being accepted.

enrichment.architecture_summary: An ontology and semantic catalog sits over relational sources in Postgres; a Next.js frontend, FastAPI services, ingestion worker, vector storage, and configurable NVIDIA NIM endpoints provide the application and model pipeline.
core_components: NVIDIA NIM inference, embedding, and reranking endpoints
enrichment.workflow: Generate or connect semantic context from enterprise metadata, resolve metrics/entities, translate natural-language questions into SQL, validate against certified definitions and lineage, and return provenance; expose context via MCP, CLI, and API.
enrichment.design_pattern: A semantic/ontology layer supplements existing customer-owned semantic models and exposes validated context to different agent harnesses.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A browsable catalog of Google product and technology Agent Skills organized by product/domain directories and installed via the skills CLI.
core_components: cloud, AI/ML, infrastructure, and developer-product guidance
enrichment.workflow: Install the repository through npx skills, choose skills, target agent and scope, then update installed skills with the skills CLI.
enrichment.design_pattern: Vendor-maintained, task-specific skill catalog distributed as agent-readable instructions rather than a single application.

sections.title: majorminorlabs/hermes-voice
sections.description: Talk to a Hermes Agent profile through Home Assistant Assist.
sections.content: A Home Assistant Assist integration for talking to a Hermes Agent profile through voice.
sections.stars_gained_note: N/A - not available from GitHub; appended as a recent-created repository, not ranked against Trending star gains
sections.why_notable: GitHub Search confirms it was created on 2026-11-05 and recently pushed; it is included as a new-repository signal, not ranked against Trending's daily star gains.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the v0.1 integration does not expose Home Assistant device-control tools by default.

enrichment.architecture_summary: A Home Assistant custom conversation integration forwards messages to a selected Hermes profile's OpenAI-compatible API while Home Assistant handles speech recognition and synthesis; an Echo Show companion screen and wake-word pipeline are also provided.
core_components: Echo Show screen and Android screen app
enrichment.workflow: Echo satellite audio enters a Home Assistant Assist pipeline; speech is transcribed, sent to the selected Hermes profile with a stable session identifier, streamed back, and spoken by the configured TTS engine.
enrichment.design_pattern: Thin Home Assistant conversation adapter that preserves profile identity and conversation history while leaving device-control tools opt-in and separate.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Composable agent skills and security workflows are represented by Cloudflare's audit skill, Matt Pocock's collection, and Google's product skills. NVIDIA Auto Ontology foregrounds grounded data and provenance for agentic analytics. Editors, shells, Rust and Python tooling, web frameworks, observability, and distributed infrastructure add a broad conventional developer-tool base. Language tally for the 15 entries: Python 4; Rust 3; JavaScript 2; TypeScript 2; Go 2; Ruby 1; Shell 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's clearest pulse is the packaging of agent expertise into reusable skills, especially for security and data-grounded work. But the rest of the list is not a wholesale shift away from conventional development: editors, language tools, web frameworks, and core infrastructure retain meaningful daily momentum. The newly created Hermes Voice project is an additional early signal for voice interfaces around agent profiles, not a daily star-gain leader.

Daily gains come from the matching Trending page; repository totals and current default-branch commit SHAs were cross-checked through REST. The recent-created Hermes Voice entry has no available daily gain figure. No prior-window comparison was collected, so no Notable Shifts section is included.
